evidence: A model result of an offline chain on the design years, A28R_301k_design_l15_snow_s934 years 10-19 on PlaSim's T21 grid, with no feedback on the climate: each 3-day mean's convective rain as point storms from a library, the large-scale rain as a steady 2 mm/h (an estimate), and Green and Ampt infiltration at lunar gravity (conductivities times g, suction heads over g) into four designed surfaces whose Earth parameters are texture-class means (Rawls et al. 1983) and a seal from Rawls et al. (1990). The Walnut Gulch library is a two-parameter family fitted to Earth's measured point storms (Osborn 1983) and the CM1 library is CM1's model storms over wet equatorial ground at 6 km and ten minutes; neither is the drylands' own storms. The soil at storm time reads PlaSim's 0.5 m bucket, which the arid, semi-arid and dry sub-humid cells keep 0.4%, 2.7% and 8% full on average. Runoff here is what leaves the point as infiltration excess; it is not routed, and nothing of it is yet lost along slopes and channels or returned by pools. The surfaces are design choices, not measured lunar soils.
reading_rule: Ratios are runoff over all rain (convective and large-scale) of the same cells and means, area-weighted over classes. walnut_gulch and cm1_6km bracket the storms' intensities from above and below; independent and continuing bracket the wetting between a mean's storms (each on the mean's soil, or one front carried through them). sealed_loam keeps a formed seal; sealed_loam_forming forms it during each storm under the lunar drops' kinetic energy. by_tenth lists the ten tenths of the lunar day from the one centred 162 degrees before noon to the one 162 after, noon falling between the fifth and sixth; null where a tenth brings under a thousandth of the cell's rain. share_of_evaporation is the runoff over the class's evaporation, an upper bound on the change of the slopes' evaporation before pools return any of it. Volumes are km3 a year of 365.25 days; storms are expected point counts.

walnut_gulch.source: Osborn (1983), WRR 19(4):1036-1042, Table 1 (fitted); Mendez, Goodrich and Osborn (2003), JAWRA 39(3):611-621, Tables 1-4 (held out)
walnut_gulch.evidence: A parametric family fitted to measured point statistics of Earth's thunderstorms at Walnut Gulch; Earth's storms, not the Moon's

cm1_6km.evidence: CM1 model result: the rain beneath each whole tracked core, its largest 6 km column at each ten-minute output; a floor on point intensities

walnut_gulch_check.rule: Set before the chain was run: it passes when the Walnut Gulch storms at Earth's gravity on the two Walnut Gulch-like soils, each storm on soil at the wilting point, give yearly runoff ratios whose span overlaps the measured 3-10% of the small watersheds; the measured geometric mean over the chain's (sandy loam and loam) is carried to the lunar bare-soil ratios as their Earth factor.

storm library.tested_by: Walnut Gulch: the family against Osborn's counts (fitted) and Mendez's annual maxima (held out); no check of the lunar storms exists until the dry box runs

wetting between storms.tested_by: none: Walnut Gulch's storms come days apart, so its runoff cannot separate the two treatments

soil at storm time.tested_by: Walnut Gulch chain at the wilting point and air-dry

surface retention.tested_by: Walnut Gulch chain (it carries the 1 mm store)

conductivity.tested_by: Walnut Gulch chain on two textures; the gravity factor analytically

suction.tested_by: Walnut Gulch chain on two textures; the gravity factor analytically

seal formation.tested_by: the seal's resistance reproduces Rawls et al.'s crust factor; the drops' energy against the rain solver

biocrust conductivity.tested_by: none beyond the measured range of reductions
